name: dterm
description: Persistent terminal sessions per workspace with auto-reattach. Self-contained — no external daemon required.

dterm.autoReconnect.description: On workspace open, recreate VS Code terminals for each live daemon session that belongs to this workspace.

dterm.scrollbackLines.description: Daemon-side scrollback retention in lines, replayed on reattach. 0 follows `terminal.integrated.scrollback` (recommended). A positive value overrides; values greater than `terminal.integrated.scrollback` will be silently truncated by xterm.js on attach.

dterm.shell.description: Override the shell executable used for new sessions. Empty = $SHELL or /bin/bash.

dterm.shellArgs.description: Arguments passed to the shell on new sessions.

dterm.tabTitle.markdownDescription:
Tab-title template for dterm terminals. When non-empty, overrides `#terminal.integrated.tabs.title#` for dterm sessions only. Empty = inherit `#terminal.integrated.tabs.title#`.

Supports the standard VS Code variables (`${process}`, `${cwd}`, `${cwdFolder}`, `${workspaceFolder}`, `${workspaceFolderName}`, `${sequence}`, `${separator}`) plus two dterm-specific additions:

- `${session}` -- the underlying dterm session id (e.g. `vscode-myproject-1`). Stable for the lifetime of the session across reattach; useful for disambiguating multiple identically-named tabs or for debugging.
- `${workspace}` -- alias for `vscode.workspace.name`. Stable across multi-root workspaces (returns the `.code-workspace` file name or single-folder name) where `${workspaceFolder}` only ever points at the first folder.

Variables that don't apply to dterm Pseudoterminals (`${task}`, `${local}`, `${shellType}`, `${shellCommand}`, `${shellPromptInput}`, `${progress}`, `${fixedDimensions}`) resolve to empty, and the surrounding `${separator}` collapses accordingly.
